# Meridian

Compact LLM context index for this repository.

Global migration law and logistics platform. TypeScript monorepo (pnpm + turbo,
Node 22, ESM). PUBLIC repo, AGPL-3.0-only. `github.com/madfam-org/meridian`.

Last updated: 2026-07-26.

## Read first

- `AGENTS.md` — canonical agent operating instructions. Read before any change.
- `packages/core/src/` — the shared contract. Read before writing code.
- `README.md` — status first, then architecture and quickstart.
- `ECOSYSTEM.md` — MADFAM ecosystem position and Enclii deployment context.
- `llms-full.txt` — full context map and durable operating contract.

## Status in one paragraph

Measured 2026-07-26 — re-verify rather than trusting it. **Twelve workspace
projects**: eight libraries under `packages/` and four deployables under
`apps/`. All twelve typecheck, test and build clean — `pnpm typecheck` 19/19,
`pnpm test` 19/19, `pnpm build` 12/12, and 103 test files carrying 2521 tests.
**All three Next.js applications now have test suites**; they had none at all
before 2026-07-26, and that was the largest gap in the repository. `apps/api` is
a running Fastify service whose image builds and starts. Four policy guards
pass; CI runs them in a `policy` job before any install. **Three of the four services are live** —
`meridian.madfam.io`, `meridian-app.madfam.io` and `meridian-admin.madfam.io`
all answered `200` on 2026-07-26 — while `meridian-api.madfam.io` answered `502`
and is not serving. Nothing has been exercised end to end. **No pathway has been
counsel-reviewed**, so `recommend()` ranks nothing. No government-system
capability is `available`.

## The three invariants

1. **Never use JavaScript `Date` for calendar arithmetic.** Use
   `@meridian/core`'s civil-date module. `DateRange` is closed and inclusive at
   both ends: 2025-01-01 to 2025-01-01 is one day.
2. **Every applied rule carries a `Citation`** — instrument, provision,
   jurisdiction, `verifiedOn`. `discretionary: true` where the source is
   administrative practice, not statute. **An instrument name is never
   translated**; use `instrumentLang()` and let it return `null` when it does
   not know.
3. **Every engine output is born disclosure-classified** —
   `information` | `assessment` | `advice`. `canRelease()` is the gate.
   Downgrading is possible; upgrading is not. Anything that ranks, orders,
   scores, or says what someone should do is `advice`.

## One page, one language

The applications used to render English and Spanish into the same elements. The
comment defending it argued for mixed-language households; the reasoning was
wrong, because a screen-reader user heard everything twice and `<html lang>`
could not be correct. Now:

- Locale lives in the URL: **English unprefixed, Spanish at `/es`**, both
  statically prerendered, with `hreflang` alternates and `x-default`. Routes are
  under `app/[locale]/` in all three Next applications.
- `@meridian/i18n` holds the contract and **depends on nothing**, not even
  `@meridian/core`, so a client component importing it cannot drag the catalog
  into the browser bundle.
- Path helpers are **asymmetric** — English has no prefix, so a hand-rolled
  `startsWith('/es')` decides `/estimate` is Spanish. Use `localizedPath`,
  `splitLocalePath`, `alternatePaths`.
- The switcher is a **server-rendered link** to the same page in the other
  locale, never to the home page.
- Catalog data stays bilingual: a `Pathway` still carries `{ en, es }`.

## Hard rules

- Do not invent law. Omit, or mark `discretionary: true` with a note.
- No marketing language, no fabricated metrics, no `TODO` for core
  functionality, no stub that throws "not implemented".
- No secrets, no credentials, no real personal data — this repo is PUBLIC.
  Every test fixture is synthetic.
- Never store, proxy or transit a government credential. Structurally refused.
- Relative imports end in `.js`. Type-only imports use `import type`.
- Workspace packages are consumed as **emitted JavaScript** from `dist/`, not as
  TypeScript source. Build before you typecheck or test across a boundary; turbo
  does this for you (`typecheck` and `test` both depend on `^build`).
- A new workspace package must be added to **all four Dockerfiles** and the
  lockfile, or the root `--frozen-lockfile` install breaks every image.
  `check-workspace-manifests.mjs` enforces this.

## Verification

```bash
cd packages/<name>        # or any of the four apps
pnpm exec tsc --noEmit
pnpm exec vitest run
```

Both must exit clean. Repo-wide, and what CI runs:

```bash
pnpm typecheck && pnpm test && pnpm build
node scripts/check-advice-boundary.mjs
node scripts/check-no-credential-custody.mjs
node scripts/check-pathway-citations.mjs
node scripts/check-workspace-manifests.mjs
```

`scripts/atlas-coverage.mjs` is a fifth script and is a **report, not a guard**.
It needs `packages/atlas/dist` built and takes `--strict` to fail on integrity
findings. It is not in CI.

`check-no-credential-custody` scans `docs/` too — documentation about the
credential refusal must **describe** the forbidden field names rather than
spelling them, or the document trips the check.

Do not run `pnpm install` or `pnpm add` while another process may be working in
the same worktree.

## Packages

Each builds with `tsc -p tsconfig.build.json`; `exports` resolves to
`./dist/index.js`. Counts measured 2026-07-26 — re-run rather than trusting.

| Package | Role | Tests |
|---|---|---|
| `@meridian/core` | civil dates, disclosure boundary, citations, tenancy, matter | 60 |
| `@meridian/mrtd` | ICAO Doc 9303 MRZ. Depends on nothing. | 111 |
| `@meridian/presence` | Schengen 90/180, tax day counts, continuous residence, work hours | 147 |
| `@meridian/pathways` | declarative rules engine (22 operations) + catalog (84, all unreviewed) | 443 |
| `@meridian/documents` | legalisation, translation, freshness, checklists, gaps | 146 |
| `@meridian/govtech` | government adapters, capability board, credential refusal | 310 |
| `@meridian/atlas` | 249 jurisdictions, 22 mobility blocs, 280 weighted corridors, coverage arithmetic. Depends on nothing. Consumed only by `scripts/atlas-coverage.mjs`. | 77 |
| `@meridian/i18n` | `Locale`, text selection, `Accept-Language` negotiation, locale paths, `instrumentLang()`. Depends on nothing. | 124 |

## Applications

| App | Role |
|---|---|
| `apps/api` | Fastify. `src/main.ts` composition root · auth (JWKS RS256) · disclosure gate + route registry + leak detector · repository ports with structural tenant scoping · append-only audit · Prisma schema (10 models, 15 enums) and an initial migration · 41 routes across 11 modules. Image builds and runs; the hostname returns 502. |
| `apps/landing` | marketing site + a working client-side Schengen 90/180 calculator, Next.js 15, dev port 3000. Catalog figures counted from `@meridian/pathways` at build time; thresholds and the Schengen citation imported from `@meridian/presence` rather than copied. Live as `meridian-landing` on meridian.madfam.io. |
| `apps/web` | applicant portal, Next.js 15, dev port 3001. `/pathways`, `/matters`, `/tools/{schengen,mrz,nationality-es}`, `/pricing`, `/for/[audience]`. Live as `meridian-app` on meridian-app.madfam.io — the package and directory keep the `web` name. |
| `apps/admin` | firm console, Next.js 15, dev port 3002. `/matters`, `/catalog`, `/audit`, `/integrations`, `/representatives`. `MERIDIAN_ASOF` pins its reference date, `MERIDIAN_ADMIN_DATASET` selects its dataset. Live as `meridian-admin`. |

All three Next applications route under `app/[locale]/` and now carry test
suites. The API's tests all run against the in-memory repository adapter; the
Prisma adapter is covered by `tsc` and nothing else, and the migration has never
been applied to a live database.

## Catalog

84 pathways — 26 Spain, 23 Canada, 35 United States — across 13 source modules
in `packages/pathways/src/catalog/`. **0 counsel-reviewed.** 449 criteria; 62 of
the 84 records can only return `requires_human_review`. 373 distinct citations,
82 `discretionary`, 347 with a URL. 63 CUSMA/USMCA professions, matching
8 CFR 214.6(c), shared by the Canadian and American routes. No pathway publishes
a processing-time estimate; no priority date, cut-off or wait estimate is
encoded anywhere.

Asylum, refugee protection and humanitarian/compassionate claims are
deliberately out of scope and will not be added.

Coverage, from `node scripts/atlas-coverage.mjs`: **1.20%** structural (3 of 249
jurisdictions) and **0.6076%** weighted by people. The stock table is 65.34%
complete against a 92.7% ceiling.

## Ecosystem

Auth via **Janua** (OIDC, RS256 JWKS, `alg: none` rejected). Billing via
**Dhanam**. Every LLM call via **Selva** at `/v1` — never a provider directly.
Compliance timestamping via **Karafiel**. Deploys via **Enclii**.

Container ports are framework defaults (3000 for the three Next apps, 8000 for
the API) and Meridian claims **no port block**. In production the number has no
effect — pods have their own network namespaces and the tunnel routes by
hostname. `ECOSYSTEM.md` has the full argument and the two cases where it does
matter; do not restate it elsewhere.

## Production operations

Routine production operations are Enclii-first. Use Enclii web, API, or CLI
before raw infrastructure tools. Direct `kubectl`, `helm`, SSH, provider CLIs,
`docker exec` or direct container access is bootstrap/break-glass only.

## Boundary

Lane C, public-safe. Private operational context — cluster access, secret
paths, operator gates, incident detail — lives in `madfam-org/internal-devops`.
When in doubt, put detail there and leave a summary plus a link here.
